newsitem.title: USA: Stericycle buys NY medical waste company.
newsitem.headline: Stericycle buys NY medical waste company.

text.p: Stericycle Inc said Monday it acquired Environmental Control Co Inc, which provides medical waste services to the New York City metropolitan area.
The acquisition is expected to increase Stericycle's annual revenues by more than $6.5 million.

As consideration for the purchase of ECCO, Stericycle said it agreed to pay about $4.2 million in cash, issue 125,000 shares of stock, assumed certain debt on trucking equipment and delivered a 10-year note for the balance of the purchase price.

Stericycle said this acquisition is an important step in its strategy of aggressively participating in the consolidation and rapid penetration of higher-margin alternate site customers in the medical waste services industry.

"From a strategic perspective, this acquisition accelerates our growth potential by establishing an excellent position in the significant New York metropolitan market," said Mark Miller, Stericycle president, in a statement.

This is the sixth acquisition the company has made since January of 1996 and the second acquisition since the company's initial public offering in August 1996, in which it raised more than $27 million.
Stericycle, the second largest provider of medical waste management services in the U.S., reported revenues of $24.5 million for its fiscal year ended December 31, 1996.
